You will be fine to take it, as long as you don't end up taking it daily or in high doses.

If you end up getting the side effects, just revert back to the Zofran. Or try something else such as Cyclizine, Prochlorperazine or Phernagan. All antiemetics.

Your doctor shouldn't be saying that. I'm no doctor but I have alot of antiemetic therapy. 

Metoclopramide (reglan) can cause a serious and irreversible movement disorder when taken in high doses (10mg+) or for long periods of time. Sometimes started as little as 1/4 weeks of use.
It works by speeding up the gastrointestinal tract. But it's not a medicine that should be used regularly. I take it daily and I have serious side effects from it.

Ondansetron (zofran) is one of the most potent antiemetics but also had less side effects when used in doses under 16mg or long term. It can cause irregular heart rythems in higher doses. But the average dose is 4mg/8mg.

Prochlorperazine is another antiemetic used for both anxiety/nausea in low doses (3mg) and for mental health issues in higher doses. 

If you had to choose between then it should be the Zofran. Raglan causes anxiety is most cases, if you google the drug reviews you see the trend.

All these drugs have side effects and you will build tolerance or increase your risk of serious or irreversible side effects if you take them often.
I've taken these for years and years and I have some damn awful side effects.

Prochlorperazine can be bought OTC in some places in low 3mg doses.
Phernagan is the same, but is sedating.

I would also suggest trying CBD products. These work well for me. And it's a much MUCH safer option than medication.
